text: Write the environment — the twelve lines that implement scope, shadowing and undefined-variable errors. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: private final Map<String,Integer> values = new HashMap<>();
void define(String name, int value) { values.put(name, value); }
if (parent != null) return ___;     // then ask the enclosing scope
explanation: Verified in the book's interpreter: `x = 100; def f(x) = x + 1; print f(1); print x;` gives 2 then 100. The order of the two clauses *is* shadowing — reverse them and parameters stop working, because the global would always win. That is how small the mechanism is, and it is the same chain Java follows to resolve a name inside a method inside a class.
